A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MATCH paper and complete supplementary material, Sections 6-14. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish identical scientific content; the only differences concern the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original segmentation experiments in Table 1, ablations in Sections 4.2 and 12, and multiclass segmentation and cell-counting results in Tables 14 and 18.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains the original segmentation benchmarks, ablations, multiclass experiments, and downstream cell-counting results, including those in the supplementary material.

M1.justification: MATCH-Pair, MATCH-Global, the teacher-student framework, and the intra- and temporal-topological consistency losses remain identical in Sections 3 and 10.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CRAG, GlaS, MoNuSeg, Roads, and MoNuSAC. Sparse/crowded nuclei scenarios, multiclass segmentation, and downstream cell counting are already present in v1 and remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: Table 1 retains MT, EM, UA-MT, URPC, XNet, PMT, TopoSemiSeg, and the fully supervised reference. Matching alternatives, LoRA-SAM/LoRA-MedSAM comparisons, and supplementary comparator sets also match.

E3.justification: Reported splits, labeled-data ratios, metrics, cropping procedures, model configurations, and training budgets are identical. Sections 8-10 retain the same dataset partitions and 12,000-iteration pretraining plus 1,000-iteration fine-tuning schedule.

E4.justification: Sections 4.2 and 12 retain the same matching and loss ablations, perturbation comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, crowding analysis, backbone comparisons, and downstream counting analysis. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The same uncertainty values and reporting practices are retained, including Table 1's significance-highlighting statement and Table 18's per-image mean and standard deviation. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-testing information changes.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1-18 and the qualitative figures are identical. For example, MATCH on CRAG with 20% labels still reports Dice_obj 0.909 ± 0.005 and BE 0.188 ± 0.018 in Table 1.

T1.justification: The matching similarity, assignment formulation, graph construction, and loss equations in Section 3 are unchanged, as are the persistent-homology definitions in supplementary Section 7. No mathematical statement or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and Section 5 conclusion retain identical claims about adaptive topological matching and dual-level consistency improving segmentation topology with limited annotations.

C2.justification: Interpretations of uncertainty, ablations, and downstream counting are unchanged. Section 13 retains the limitations concerning feature stability, noisy predictions, and computational overhead; Section 14's impact discussion also matches.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, training-time and memory figures, and code-access information are identical. The updated arXiv self-link provides no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 85 references are unchanged, including the positioning relative to TopoSemiSeg, Wasserstein matching, and Betti Matching.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal stamp changes from arXiv:2510.01532v1, dated 2 Oct 2025, to arXiv:2510.01532v2, dated 2 Jun 2026. Body wording, author information, headings, and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-6 and Tables 1-18 retain identical formatting, captions, and placement. Rendered pages 2-20 match exactly, and page 1 differs only within the version/date stamp, without a layout revision.

improvement.justification: Only the arXiv version/date stamp and associated self-link change. The main paper and supplementary material retain identical methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
